text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- National Association of Metallurgical companies says half of the sectors' 15,000 companies in the sector may disappear in the next five years because of outdated technology.

- President of glass company Barbosa e Almeida Maria Candida Morais says it will invest eight billion escudos in a factory in Spain's Estremadura to strengthen its position as number two in the Iberian market.
- President of Portugal's Audit Court Alfredo Jose de Sousa says parliament does poor job of financially controlling the government.
- Chairman of ADtranz unit Manuel Norton says his consortium, which includes ABB and Soares da Costa, could invite Siemens to join if it wins bidding to supply coaches for Oporto metro.
- Planning Minister Joao Cravinho said the impact of European Union financing on economic growth in 1994/1996 was an average 0.9 percent, around a third of overall growth.

- An indefinite strike called by workers at at copper company Somincor may bring production to a total halt at the Neves Corvo mines after three or four days, director of Human Resources Raul Araujo said. Workers are protesting against working on Sundays.
